title: Regional changes in ozone by warmth slopes had no clear difference in selected US bird surveys in 1995-2024
abstract: We tested whether an ozone by seasonal warmth slope changed more in the western US than in the eastern US. We reused a signed bird-richness panel and four models for East and West in 1995-2009 and 2010-2024. State score sums allowed errors to be shared across periods. The western late-minus-early change was +0.776 recorded species per 10 ppb ozone and 2 C warmth. The eastern change was -0.231. Their difference was +1.006, with an approximate interval of -0.520 to +2.533 after adjustment for three contrasts. The direct test did not establish a regional difference in temporal change. It did not establish equal changes. Route trends, common-route selection and nearby-monitor checks are reported. This is an exploratory contrast of associations in reused records. It is not independent biological validation or a causal climate-change test. Few western states, high leverage, shared annual errors, coarse exposure and observation bias limit inference. The package has code, aggregate evidence, a figure and a verified retrieval recipe. Survey-level records remain external.

display.caption: Changes in fitted ozone by warmth slopes between 1995-2009 and 2010-2024. Bars give approximate intervals adjusted for three direct contrasts within each model. These are associations in selected US bird surveys.
